instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Use NASA’s website as the source of truth (no sign-in/registration)
criteria.description: Rely on information from NASA-controlled pages (nasa.gov or official NASA subdomains) to determine the next planned Artemis mission and its details. Full credit if the agent uses NASA pages and does not sign in/register. Full credit also if the agent attempts to use NASA.gov but access is blocked/down (e.g., CAPTCHA, outage) and the agent clearly reports the limitation. Partial credit if the agent references non-NASA sources only as secondary context while still treating NASA as authoritative.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 and Screenshot 2 both show nasa.gov pages with NASA branding (NASA logo and standard nav). Neither screenshot shows any sign-in/login wall or registration/updates prompt being used. Action history URLs are on nasa.gov (Artemis overview and Artemis II mission page). Latest is Screenshot 2 (Artemis II page), also with no sign-in/registration.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent used NASA’s website (nasa.gov) as the source and did not sign in or register. Screenshots support this directly, so the baseline score stands.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a NASA.gov page with the NASA “meatball” logo in the top navigation and a page titled “Artemis II.” The top nav includes “News & Events,” “Multimedia,” and “NASA+ LIVE,” and a program nav row listing “Artemis,” “Artemis I,” “Artemis II,” “Artemis III,” and “Artemis IV.” No login, sign-in prompts, or registration/updates forms are visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This screenshot supports that the agent is using NASA’s official website (NASA.gov) as the source and is not signing in or registering. That satisfies the constraint portion of the criterion based on what’s visible.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy visible regarding source/registration: the page appears to be on NASA.gov and shows no sign-in/registration flow.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a NASA.gov page with the NASA “meatball” logo at top center and a navigation bar including “News & Events,” “Multimedia,” and “NASA+ LIVE.” A mission navigation row shows “Artemis,” “Artemis I,” “Artemis II,” “Artemis III,” and “Artemis IV.” The page headline reads “Artemis,” with descriptive text beginning “Under Artemis, NASA will send astronauts…” There is no sign-in prompt, registration form, or login wall visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This supports that the agent is using NASA’s website (NASA branding and Artemis navigation are visible) and there is no evidence of signing in or registering on-screen. However, the screenshot itself does not show the specific mission-detail source (e.g., Artemis II page content), only the Artemis overview page.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output references details like “LaunchED April 1, 2026” and Artemis II specifics, but the screenshot only shows the Artemis overview header and general program description, not Artemis II mission details or any launch date text.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot/DOM state index 2 (LATEST) shows the agent on https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-ii/ (NASA-controlled domain) with mission content visible. No sign-in, registration, or update-registration flow/modal is shown in this DOM snapshot. Earlier states (0,1) also remain on nasa.gov, but state 2 is the strongest/most direct evidence for sourcing mission facts from NASA without authentication.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Baseline 3/3 remains correct. The latest screenshot confirms the agent used an official NASA.gov mission page as the information source and did not sign in or register (no such flows are evidenced).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 shows URL "https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-ii/" (NASA.gov) and page title "Artemis II: NASA’s First Crewed Lunar Flyby in 50 Years - NASA". The visible content includes mission facts like "Mission Type" and "LaunchED" without any sign-in/registration modal or form in the captured nodes.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The active page in the final state is a NASA-controlled nasa.gov mission page (State 2 URL). The DOM snapshot contains mission information and navigation but no evidence of sign-in/registration steps being taken or required. This satisfies using NASA’s website as the source of truth under the given constraints.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None observed in the provided DOM snapshot regarding source-of-truth or sign-in/registration requirements.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows URL `https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/artemis/` (a nasa.gov page) and NASA primary navigation; no sign-in/registration prompts are shown in the visible content snippet.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The provided DOM evidence confirms the agent is on a NASA-controlled site (nasa.gov) and interacting with Artemis content. However, the agent’s reported mission details are attributed to another page (State 2 per action history) whose DOM is not included, so NASA-as-source-of-truth for the *specific details* cannot be fully verified from the provided DOM. Also, while no sign-in/registration elements are visible in DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1, the absence of such flows cannot be proven beyond the captured snippet.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history references State 2 (`https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-ii/`) as the source of mission details, but no DOM snapshot for State 2 is provided, limiting verification that the reported details were taken from NASA pages. No explicit DOM evidence that sign-in/registration was avoided beyond the shown content.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows URL "https://www.nasa.gov/" (NASA-controlled domain). Action history states the agent navigated to "https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/artemis/" (State 1) and then "https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-ii/" (State 2), both NASA-controlled pages.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The available DOM evidence confirms use of NASA.gov as the browsing context (DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 URL is nasa.gov) and the action history indicates subsequent navigation stayed on nasa.gov mission pages (Artemis hub and Artemis II mission page). However, the DOM evidence provided does not include States 1–2 content, so it cannot directly verify that the mission details were sourced from NASA page text (only that navigation occurred to NASA URLs). There is also no DOM evidence showing any sign-in/registration flow; given the limited DOM snapshot, absence of such UI cannot be proven, but the recorded actions are simple link clicks and do not involve authentication or registration.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: DOM snapshot coverage is only for DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 (NASA homepage). No DOM content is provided for State 1 (Artemis page) or State 2 (Artemis II page), so the rubric requirement to use NASA as “source of truth” for the specific mission details cannot be fully validated from DOM evidence alone.

criteria.criterion: Identify the next planned Artemis mission and report required mission details
criteria.description: Correctly determine which Artemis mission is the next planned/upcoming one according to NASA’s website and report: (1) mission name, (2) planned launch year (or NASA-stated target/window with the year), (3) destination, and (4) primary objective as NASA describes it. Full credit if all four fields are correctly captured from NASA pages. If NASA presents ambiguous/updated information across pages (e.g., differing target dates), full credit if the agent notes the discrepancy and reports the most recently published/most clearly designated 'next' mission details. Partial credit if the agent identifies the correct next mission but one or more fields are missing/overly vague. No credit if the mission selected is clearly not the next planned one per NASA.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 2 (latest) shows the Artemis II mission page with: mission name 'Artemis II', mission type 'Crewed Lunar Flyby', and descriptive text about being the first crewed Artemis flight. It also shows 'LAUNCHED — April 1, 2026' and 'SPLASHDOWN — April 10, 2026' plus 'OCCURRED 5 MONTHS AGO', indicating Artemis II is presented as already completed, not upcoming/planned. Screenshot 1 is only the Artemis program page and does not show 'next planned mission' details.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: While the agent correctly extracted fields that are visible on the Artemis II page (name, launch year from the displayed launched date, mission type/destination, and the short objective description), they failed the key requirement: identifying the 'next planned Artemis mission.' The latest screenshot explicitly indicates Artemis II already occurred ('OCCURRED 5 MONTHS AGO' and 'LAUNCHED'), so it cannot be supported as the next planned/upcoming mission based on NASA’s site as shown. This is a critical error in mission selection, so the score should be substantially reduced, but not to zero because the reported fields for Artemis II are largely supported by the screenshot.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Visible on the Artemis II page: the heading “Artemis II.” A short description reads: “The first crewed Artemis flight marks a key step toward long-term return to the Moon and future missions to Mars.” A facts area shows labels/values including “MISSION TYPE — Crewed Lunar Flyby,” “MISSION DURATION — 9 Days, 1 Hour, 32 Minutes,” “LAUNCHED — April 1, 2026,” and “SPLASHDOWN — April 10, 2026.”
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot provides strong support for mission name (Artemis II), destination/type (“Crewed Lunar Flyby”), and the year from the displayed launch date (April 1, 2026). It also provides NASA-stated objective text about being the first crewed Artemis flight and a step toward returning to the Moon and future Mars missions. However, the task asks for the “next planned Artemis mission.” The screenshot indicates Artemis II has already “LAUNCHED” and also says “OCCURRED 5 MONTHS AGO,” so from this page alone it is not clearly the next planned/upcoming mission; it appears to be a past mission. Therefore, the agent’s choice of Artemis II as “next planned” is not supported by the screenshot and is likely incorrect under the criterion’s ‘next planned’ requirement.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output calls Artemis II “the next planned Artemis mission,” but the screenshot explicitly shows “OCCURRED 5 MONTHS AGO” and a “LAUNCHED” date, implying it is not upcoming/planned. The agent also states “Destination: Crewed lunar flyby of the Moon,” which aligns with “MISSION TYPE — Crewed Lunar Flyby” shown. The agent’s objective statement is consistent with the visible description sentence.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Visible text includes the large title “Artemis” and a program description: “Under Artemis, NASA will send astronauts on increasingly difficult missions to explore more of the Moon for scientific discovery, economic benefits, and to build on our foundation for the first crewed missions to Mars.” The top mission tabs list “Artemis I,” “Artemis II,” “Artemis III,” and “Artemis IV,” but no mission-specific panel is open and no launch year, destination, or primary objective for a specific mission is shown in the visible content.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot does not contain the required details for the “next planned Artemis mission” (mission name, planned launch year, destination, primary objective). While Artemis II is listed in the navigation, the screenshot provides no evidence that Artemis II is the next planned mission or any of the specific fields requested. Therefore, the agent’s predicted output cannot be validated against this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output claims Artemis II is the next planned mission with a planned launch year of 2026 and specifies destination and objective. None of those specific facts (2026, lunar flyby, “first crewed Artemis flight” wording) are visible in the screenshot; only the general Artemis program description is visible.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot/DOM state index 2 (LATEST) explicitly shows: mission name 'Artemis II'; 'Mission Type' = 'Crewed Lunar Flyby'; 'LaunchED' = 'April 1, 2026' (year 2026 visible); and description text: 'The first crewed Artemis flight marks a key step toward long‑term return to the Moon and future missions to Mars.' Screenshot/DOM state index 1 shows Artemis mission navigation (Artemis I/II/III/IV) but does not label which is 'next planned.' No screenshot explicitly states Artemis II is the 'next planned Artemis mission.'
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The agent correctly reported the mission name and launch year as shown in the latest DOM, and the primary objective is supported by the mission description line shown. However, two key gaps remain per the DOM rule: (a) 'next planned' is not explicitly confirmed by the provided DOM (no 'next'/'upcoming' designation captured), and (b) 'destination' is not explicitly presented as a destination field; the DOM supports 'Mission Type: Crewed Lunar Flyby' and mentions 'return to the Moon,' but does not explicitly state 'Destination: the Moon' in a mission-facts field. Award strong partial credit because 3 of 4 required details are explicitly supported and the remaining parts are not fully confirmed by the DOM.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 includes: "Artemis II"; "Mission Type" -> "Crewed Lunar Flyby"; "LaunchED" -> "April 1, 2026"; and the description line "The first crewed Artemis flight marks a key step toward long‑term return to the Moon and future missions to Mars."
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM explicitly supports key required fields for Artemis II: mission name ("Artemis II"), launch timing including year ("LaunchED" "April 1, 2026"), and a NASA-stated objective/summary ("The first crewed Artemis flight marks a key step toward long‑term return to the Moon and future missions to Mars."). However, the agent’s claimed "Destination: Crewed lunar flyby of the Moon" is not explicitly stated as "destination" in the captured DOM; the page shows "Mission Type: Crewed Lunar Flyby" but does not explicitly include the word "Moon" as the destination in the visible mission facts (though "return to the Moon" appears in the objective line). Also, the DOM snapshot alone does not prove that Artemis II is the *next planned* Artemis mission (it does not show a "next" label or a comparison against Artemis I/III/IV scheduling).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies:
1) "Next planned Artemis mission": Not explicitly evidenced in DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 (no "next"/"upcoming" designation captured).
2) "Destination": Agent states "lunar flyby of the Moon"; DOM shows "Mission Type: Crewed Lunar Flyby" and separately mentions "return to the Moon" in the objective line, but does not explicitly present a destination field equating to "Moon" in the captured mission facts.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 includes Artemis mission navigation items such as `Artemis I`, `Artemis II`, `Artemis III`, and `Artemis IV`, but does not display launch year, destination, or primary objective text for Artemis II in the visible content provided.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
The DOM evidence provided (State 1 only) shows that Artemis II exists as a navigation item, but it does not contain the required details (planned launch year, destination, primary objective) nor does it establish that Artemis II is the *next planned* mission. The agent’s answer cites specifics (e.g., a 2026 launch date and objective phrasing) that would need to be verified from the Artemis II mission page (State 2), but that DOM snapshot is not available here.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims: launch year 2026, destination crewed lunar flyby, and a specific primary objective statement. None of these are supported or contradicted by DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1; they are simply unverified due to missing DOM evidence for State 2.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 provides no Artemis mission detail fields (launch year, destination, primary objective) and does not show the Artemis II mission page content. It only contains a homepage highlight mentioning "President Honors Artemis II Crew" and the label "ARTEMIS II" in the visible content.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: UNKNOWN
The agent’s reported answer asserts: Artemis II; planned launch year 2026; destination crewed lunar flyby; primary objective described as first crewed Artemis flight to test human deep space capabilities. None of these required fields (launch year, destination, objective) are present in the provided DOM evidence (DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 is the NASA homepage, not the Artemis II mission detail page). The action history indicates the agent clicked to the Artemis II mission page (State 2: https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-ii/), but without DOM for State 2, the correctness of the extracted launch year/destination/objective and even whether Artemis II is presented as the “next planned” mission cannot be confirmed or refuted from the DOM-model evidence provided.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s answer includes specific details (e.g., "LaunchED April 1, 2026") that are not verifiable from DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0. Because the DOM for the Artemis II page is not included, the analysis cannot confirm whether NASA currently states that specific date/year, the destination phrasing, or the primary objective wording.

criteria.criterion: Stop after recording the required mission details
criteria.description: Stop promptly after obtaining and reporting the mission name, planned launch year, destination, and primary objective. Full credit if the agent stops once the required information is recorded, allowing minimal additional navigation only to resolve ambiguity or confirm a conflicting detail on NASA.gov. Partial credit if the agent continues browsing beyond what is reasonably needed but still provides the correct required details.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action history shows navigation from the Artemis overview page to the Artemis II mission page and no further actions recorded. Screenshot 2 is the last state shown and contains the mission facts area the agent used to report details. There is no evidence of additional browsing beyond what’s shown.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Based on the recorded action history and the screenshots, the agent stopped after reaching a mission page and outputting the requested fields (even though the chosen mission was not actually the next planned one). This criterion measures stopping behavior, not correctness of the mission selection, so the baseline score remains appropriate.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Only one page state is visible: the NASA Artemis II mission page with mission facts (mission type, duration, launched, splashdown) and the descriptive sentence. There is no visible evidence of continued browsing beyond this page within the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot alone cannot confirm whether the agent stopped promptly after collecting required details, but it does show the agent on a page with the relevant fields (name, launch date/year, mission type/destination, objective text). There is no evidence in the screenshot of unnecessary additional navigation. Partial support for stopping condition, but overall task completion is undermined by the apparent misidentification of “next planned” mission.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No direct discrepancy about continued browsing can be established from a single screenshot; however, the agent’s reported stopping after identifying Artemis II conflicts with the screenshot suggesting Artemis II already occurred.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Only a single NASA Artemis overview page is shown with the title “Artemis” and site navigation; there is no indication in the screenshot of additional browsing steps beyond this page, nor any visible “recorded” mission details on-screen.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: From the screenshot alone, it’s not possible to determine whether the agent stopped promptly after obtaining the required details, because the screenshot doesn’t show the details being gathered or any subsequent unnecessary navigation. The agent’s predicted output suggests they did stop after providing details, but that behavior is not verifiable here.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No direct discrepancy about continued browsing can be confirmed from this screenshot; however, the screenshot does not show the point at which the agent collected the mission details they reported.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Action history ends after reaching State 2. Screenshot/DOM state index 2 (LATEST) shows the Artemis II mission page as the final state with no further navigation evidenced.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Baseline 2/2 stands. The agent stopped after reaching the Artemis II page and providing the required fields (even if some are only partially supported under criterion 1). No unnecessary additional browsing is evidenced after obtaining mission facts.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 is the final state at "https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-ii/" and the prompt’s 'Agent predicted output' reports the four requested details without any further states/actions shown after Action 2.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
Based on the provided action history, the agent navigated to the Artemis II mission page (State 2) and then produced the requested output. No additional browsing actions beyond reaching the mission page are shown, aligning with the stopping condition to stop after recording the required details.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None with respect to stopping behavior; the history ends at State 2 / Action 2 and the agent provides an output.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 only shows the Artemis program page and does not show subsequent browsing beyond the Artemis navigation; action history indicates the agent clicked into Artemis II and then produced an answer.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
Based on the action history, the agent navigated to Artemis II and then provided the requested four fields without additional browsing, which aligns with the stopping condition. However, because only DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 is provided, the evaluator cannot fully confirm from DOM evidence alone that the agent stopped immediately after collecting the required details (i.e., cannot verify no further navigation or additional pages beyond the recorded actions).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: DOM evidence is incomplete (no State 2 snapshot), so the stop point can only be inferred from action history rather than verified via DOM snapshots.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 plus action history shows two clicks (to Artemis page, then Artemis II page) and the agent produced a final set of four requested fields in the "Agent predicted output" section.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
Based on the action history, the agent navigated to the Artemis II page and then provided exactly the requested items (mission name, launch year, destination, primary objective) without any recorded additional browsing/actions beyond opening Artemis II. However, since only DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 is available, we cannot fully verify whether additional navigation occurred within State 2 or beyond what is shown in the action history; still, within the provided record, the stopping behavior appears consistent with stopping after obtaining the needed details.
